articles.title: Electrophysiological properties of mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive.
articles.authors: Stijn Voerman, Xiang Wang, Xiaolu Wang et al.
articles.abstract: The neocortex has the largest volume, whereas the cerebellum houses the most neurons of the mammalian brain, underscoring paramount functions for interactions between them. Neocortical projections to the cerebellum involve both the mossy fibre and climbing fibre systems; mossy fibres find their origin predominantly in the pons, whereas the climbing fibres are relayed via subnuclei of the inferior olive (IO) that receive cortical input via the mesodiencephalic junction (MDJ). Given that climbing fibres regulate cerebellar plasticity in a timing-dependent manner, the MDJ-IO pathway probably contributes to both sensorimotor and cognitive learning. However, the physiological properties of IO-projecting MDJ neurons remain largely unknown. Here, we made targeted whole-cell recordings in brain slices of the mouse MDJ, separating IO- from non-IO-projecting neurons following retrograde tracing. We show that IO-projecting neurons are, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, highly spontaneously active and capable of high-frequency bursts of ≤350 Hz during current injections. Optogenetic stimulation shows that excitatory neocortical inputs to IO-projecting MDJ neurons can be integrated directly with excitatory inputs from the cerebellar nuclei. Moreover, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, IO-projecting MDJ neurons depolarize and repolarize quickly, and hyperpolarizing inputs consistently trigger rebound action potentials upon stimulus offset. This hyperpolarization is probably induced predominantly by inhibitory inputs from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey, which provide prominent bilateral inputs to MDJ neurons, as revealed by viral tracing in Gad2-Cre mice. Our results highlight how neocortical inputs to the MDJ can be transformed into diverse IO firing patterns and thereby contribute to the required specifics of cerebellar learning. KEY POINTS: The mesodiencephalic junction is an important brainstem region connecting the cerebral cortex with the cerebellum through its projection to the inferior olive, the sole source of the climbing fibres that drive cerebellar learning. We find that mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive represent a population of physiologically distinct neurons, capable of high firing frequencies and rebound activity following hyperpolarization. We reveal that mesodiencephalic junction neurons receive prominent excitatory inputs from neocortex and cerebellar nuclei, whereas their main inhibitory inputs are derived from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey. These findings shed light on how the activity of neurons in the mesodiencephalic junction can be regulated and how these neurons might influence activity in the inferior olive, and thereby cerebellar learning.

articles.title: Combined time-restricted feeding and resistance training enhance tirzepatide-induced improvements in adiposity and whole-body insulin sensitivity in female mice.
articles.authors: Ana Paula Azevêdo Macêdo, Luciana Renata da Conceição de Mattis, Robson Damasceno de Lima et al.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide is a dual agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors with potent effects on body weight regulation, glucose homeostasis and metabolic health. However, its interaction with dietary and exercise interventions as well as its impact on obesity and hepatic metabolic pathways, particularly in females, remain unclear. Here, we tested whether tirzepatide, alone or combined with time-restricted feeding (TRF) or resistance training, modulates energy balance, strength performance, adipose tissue remodelling, insulin sensitivity and hepatic lipid accumulation in female mice. Female Swiss mice after 10 weeks of obesity induction were treated with tirzepatide, TRF or resistance training for 8 weeks. Tirzepatide was administered subcutaneously using a dose-escalation protocol. TRF consisted of a 12 h feeding window, and resistance training was performed as stair climbing on alternating days. Body weight, caloric intake and feed efficiency were monitored longitudinally. Glucose homeostasis was assessed by intraperitoneal glucose and insulin tolerance tests. Adipose depots, skeletal muscle and liver mass were quantified, and hepatic lipid accumulation was evaluated by histology and RT-qPCR of lipogenic metabolism genes. Tirzepatide reduced body weight gain and feed efficiency, consistent with a negative energy balance. When combined with TRF and resistance training, tirzepatide accelerated weight loss, and the addition of resistance training further enhanced this effect, bringing body weight close to control levels. These effects were associated with reduced adipose mass and adipocyte hypertrophy, indicating improved adipose tissue remodelling. Resistance training improved strength performance and increased skeletal muscle mass. Tirzepatide combined with TRF, with or without resistance training, improved glucose tolerance in female mice. All interventions reduced hepatic lipid accumulation. Collectively, tirzepatide, particularly in combination with TRF and resistance training, exerts enhanced metabolic benefits on obesity, insulin sensitivity and metabolic regulation in female mice. KEY POINTS: Tirzepatide combined with time-restricted feeding and resistance training produced greater reductions in body weight and adiposity in obese female mice. Combined interventions improved whole-body insulin sensitivity more effectively than isolated strategies. Resistance training preserved skeletal muscle mass during tirzepatide-induced weight loss. All interventions similarly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and lipogenic gene expression. Tirzepatide-based therapies enhanced systemic metabolic health without additional hepatic benefits from combined interventions.

articles.title: Persistent Skeletal Deficits Following Weight Restoration in a Rodent Model of Anorexia Nervosa.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Malihe Jafari, Daniel J Brooks, Benton Swanson et al.
articles.abstract: Purpose: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with significant changes in bone density and microstructure. However, the extent and nature of skeletal recovery following weight restoration is unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate these changes in bone during simulated AN in rats across short- and long-term recovery. Methods: Female Sprague Dawley rats were exposed to 50-60% food restriction for 30 days to simulate AN, followed by recovery periods of 5, 15, and 30 days. Bone parameters were assessed longitudinally using peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) and micro-computed tomography (µCT). Bodyweight and muscle strength were correlated with bone parameters. Results: AN resulted in significant reductions in total and trabecular bone density, as well as impairments in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture. Even with weight restoration, these deficits persisted and the compensatory responses were not sufficient for bone recovery. Bodyweight showed an association with total and trabecular bone density. Measures of muscle strength also correlated with total and trabecular density and were additive in multiple regression analysis prediction of total and trabecular bone density when combined with bodyweight. Conclusion: Recovery from AN-induced bone disorders is incomplete even after weight restoration and likely requires targeted interventions beyond nutritional rehabilitation. Furthermore, muscle function is an important predictor of bone health when combined with bodyweight.

articles.title: Blood lactate concentrations are associated with markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Regis C Pearson, Destiny P Hamilton, Nicholas T Broskey et al.
articles.abstract: The ability to detect metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy can impact the health of mother and infant(s). Lactate may serve as a biomarker to predict metabolic dysfunction risk. The purpose of this study was to determine if fasting or postprandial blood lactate concentrations were related to established markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy. Overnight fasted healthy women between 32-38 weeks gestation underwent a high-fat meal test. Fasted and postprandial (1h, 2h, and 4h) venous blood glucose, insulin, and lactate were collected. Fasted and postprandial (2h and 4h) respiratory exchange ratios (RERs) were assessed by indirect calorimetry. HOMA-IR and Matsuda indexes were calculated. Participants were categorized into lean (18.5-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), or obese (≥30.0 kg/m2) based on pre-pregnancy body mass index. To determine the impact that weight status may have on postprandial lactate concentrations, a repeated-measures analysis of variance was performed on log-transformed data. Spearman's rank-order correlation coefficients were used to assess associations between outcome variables. 52 participants were included in the analysis (lean, n = 29; overweight, n = 11; obese, n = 12). Postprandial lactate was higher in women with obesity compared to women who were lean (1h, p = 0.024; 2h, p = 0.025; 4h, p = 0.010). Among all women, higher lactate area under the curve (AUC) was associated with higher insulin AUC, higher HOMA-IR index, lower Matsuda index, and higher RER AUC (p ≤ 0.003). These findings suggest that postprandially elevated lactate may serve as a useful biomarker for identifying metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy.

articles.title: One Carbon Metabolism - The Missing Link for Cancer and Sepsis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Abigail Anderson, Carter Weeg
articles.abstract: One-carbon (1C) metabolism (OCM) is a biosynthetic and physiological process essential to cells. OCM encompasses a multitude of tightly regulated biochemical reactions that are responsible for nucleotide synthesis (purines and pyrimidines), amino acid homeostasis (Met, Ser, Gly), redox balance, and epigenetic regulation. Dysregulations of this pathway have been implicated in the development and progression of cancer and sepsis - two complex pathologies, each with a characteristically high morbidity and mortality rate. OCM changes in the oncogenic state have been extensively investigated, while metabolic pathway changes in sepsis remain more elusive. Given that emerging evidence suggests that 1 in 5 sepsis hospitalizations occur in patients with a cancer diagnosis, and recovering sepsis patients have a higher incidence of cancer diagnosis, our review aims to analyze the known OCM changes that occur in each pathology, highlight commonalities and variations, and suggest clinical implications that explore possible therapeutic targets. Through a novel cross-disease examination, a more comprehensive understanding of OCM metabolic changes in these disease states could inform clinical practice and lead to the development of targeted therapeutic interventions that further our understanding and treatment of one or both conditions.

articles.title: Longitudinal Analysis of Skeletal Muscle and Cardiometabolic Risk During the Menopause Transition.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Hannah E Cabre, Kaja Falkenhain, Steve R Smith et al.
articles.abstract: We assessed longitudinal changes in body composition and cardiometabolic risk in those with normal-weight and overweight/obese women across the menopausal transition. We examined a 10-year longitudinal analysis of 81 healthy women in the prospective Healthy Transitions cohort. Body composition measures were obtained via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Skeletal muscle was estimated using a validated prediction model: 1.12 × appendicular lean mass- 0.63. Serum sex steroid hormones and cardiometabolic factors were quantified in fasting blood. Participants were stratified by BMI into normal weight (n=41) and overweight/obesity (n=40) groups. Changes within and between BMI groups across the menopause transition were assessed with linear mixed models. At menopause onset, compared to those with normal weight, participants with overweight/obesity had lower sex hormone-binding globulin (-30.9±10.3 nmol/L; p=0.01), greater percent body fat (13.1±1.3%; p<0.001), greater skeletal muscle mass (2.5±0.6 kg; p<0.001), and worse cardiometabolic risk factors (p<0.001). In the 5 years before menopause, participants with overweight/obesity gained skeletal muscle (+1.2 kg) and fat mass (+3.5 kg), while participants with normal weight increased percent body fat (+1.5%) only. At menopause onset, women with overweight/obesity exhibit distinct alterations in body composition, hormonal profiles, and cardiometabolic risk that exist in the years preceding menopause, highlighting the importance of early, targeted interventions to mitigate adverse health trajectories during the menopause transition.

articles.title: Platelet Mitochondrial Bioenergetics in Adolescents at Risk of MASLD Following High-Intensity Interval Training.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Jeny E Rivera, Emir Tas, Craig Porter et al.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent cardiometabolic disorder in adolescents with obesity associated with insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Platelets contribute to inflammatory and vascular processes implicated in cardiometabolic disease, yet little is known regarding platelet mitochondrial bioenergetics in adolescents at risk for MASLD or their response to exercise training. This study characterized platelet mitochondrial respiration in adolescents at risk of MASLD and examined the effects of four weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) according to MASLD status (n=10 MASLD; n=17 non-MASLD). MASLD was defined as intrahepatic triglyceride (IHTG) content ≥5% by magnetic resonance imaging. Platelet mitochondrial respiration was assessed at enrollment and after four weeks of supervised HIIT using high-resolution respirometry. Associations with cardiometabolic and fitness markers were examined using Spearman correlations, and longitudinal changes following HIIT were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Adolescents were 15.4±1.5 years old and 48% were boys. At enrollment, adolescents with MASLD had higher IHTG than those without MASLD (7.39±2.67% vs. 3.02±1.13%, p=0.0002). Maximal electron transfer capacity was positively associated with IHTG (rho=0.50, p=0.008) and HOMA-IR (rho=0.44, p=0.021) and inversely associated with leptin (rho=-0.60, p=0.001). Adolescents with MASLD exhibited higher NADH-linked respiration (β=0.053, p=0.033) and succinate-supported respiration (β=0.070, p=0.012). Significant time-by-MASLD interactions demonstrated reductions in both respiration measures following HIIT only in adolescents with MASLD. In conclusion, platelet mitochondrial respiration was associated with hepatic fat content and markers of metabolic dysfunction in adolescents with obesity. HIIT was associated with differential platelet bioenergetic adaptations according to MASLD status.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.
articles.authors: Gabriel Matheus Da Silva Batista, Ighor Luiz Azevedo Teixeira, Ednei Luiz Antonio et al.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on lean mass, muscle size and muscle performance during immobilisation and rehabilitation: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Jedd Pratt, Darren G Candow, Eric S Rawson et al.
articles.abstract: Creatine monohydrate (CrM) supplementation has established benefits in exercising populations; however, its efficacy during disuse and subsequent rehabilitation remains unclear. This systematic review assessed the effects of CrM supplementation on muscle size, lean mass and muscle performance (strength, power, endurance) during periods of disuse and rehabilitation. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Six randomised placebo-controlled trials were included (n = 118, mean ages: 15-24 years, disuse model: 1-2 weeks limb-immobilisation). Two studies reported comparable reductions in quadriceps cross-sectional area (CSA; assessed via CT or NMR imaging) between CrM and placebo during disuse (-5.6% vs. -5.5%; -11.0% vs. -9.4%), whereas two reported smaller reductions from CrM supplementation in lower-limb lean mass (-5.6% vs. -8.9%) or preserved upper-limb lean mass (0.9% vs. -3.7%) (assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) or dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)). These contrasting findings may reflect limitations of BIA/DXA, including hydration effects, rather than preservation of muscle tissue. Effects on muscle performance were inconsistent, with favourable findings from CrM supplementation in upper- but not lower-limb models. Four studies included recovery, three of which used resistance-based rehabilitation. Two reported greater increases with CrM supplementation across quadriceps CSA (21.3% vs. 14.3%), lower-limb lean mass (5.6% vs. 3.8%), power (52.2% vs. 35.2%) and strength (28.7% vs. 22.8%). Current evidence does not unanimously support CrM supplementation as an effective countermeasure to mitigate disuse-induced muscle atrophy, lean mass loss or declines in muscle performance. Whether CrM supplementation meaningfully influences rehabilitation following disuse, particularly in older adults and clinical populations at greater risk of disuse atrophy and incomplete recovery, warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Simultaneous acquisition of maternal and dual-fetal electrocardiography with maternal haemodynamic monitoring in anaesthetized pregnant rats.
articles.authors: Sarah Pribil Pardun, Spencer Duff, Payton Ward et al.
articles.abstract: Experimental approaches that acquire maternal haemodynamics together with direct cardiac signals from more than one fetus remain limited. We developed a standardized in vivo method for simultaneous acquisition of maternal ECG, maternal arterial blood pressure and ECGs from two fetuses in anaesthetized late-gestation Sprague-Dawley rats. The platform combines custom-fabricated needle electrodes with conventional cardiovascular instrumentation and PowerLab/LabChart acquisition. Stable, analysable maternal arterial blood pressure, maternal ECG and dual-fetal ECG were maintained for ≤5 h. The recordings supported beat-to-beat ECG interval and heart rate variability analyses. Fetuses had lower heart rates and longer R-R intervals than dams, and fetal root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), high-frequency power and standard deviation of RR intervals (SDRR) were lower than maternal values. As proof of recording responsiveness, maternal noradrenaline and verapamil administration produced readily resolved maternal haemodynamic changes together with time-aligned fetal heart rate responses. This protocol does not by itself demonstrate maternal-fetal cardiac coupling; rather, it provides synchronized high-resolution signals suitable for future analyses of dynamic maternal-fetal cardiovascular relationships and pharmacological responses.

articles.title: Effects of acetaminophen ingestion on the torque-duration relationship and fatigability during intermittent exercise in patients with type 1 diabetes.
articles.authors: Nadia Fekih, Amal Machfer, Achraf Ammar et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effects of acute ingestion of acetaminophen (ACT) on the magnitude of exercise-induced peripheral fatigue (ΔPtw) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D). In a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind design, 22 males (11 T1D and 11 control (CTR) completed 60 maximum voluntary contractions 60 min after ingesting 1 g of acetaminophen (ACT) or 1 g of placebo (PL) on two separate visits. Central and peripheral fatigue were assessed from pre- to post-exercise changes in quadriceps voluntary activation (ΔVA) and potentiated twitch force (ΔPtw), respectively. Critical torque (CT) was defined as the mean force produced during the final 12 contractions, and work performed (W') was computed as the impulse performed above CT. Maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), VA and Ptw decreased after exercise in both groups, with no significant difference between PL and ACT condition. Compared to PL, ACT increased root mean square/Mmax and CT values in the T1D (+21% and 8% respectively) and CTR groups (+40% and +19%; respectively), with significant lower effect in the T1D compared to the CTR group (P < 0.05). No significant effect of ACT was observed for W' in the T1D (+7%) and CTR groups (+4%) (P = 0.68). These findings indicate that acute ACT ingestion increased CT and muscle activation during the repeated-MVC protocol in both groups, although the magnitude of these responses was smaller in the T1D than the CTR group.

articles.title: Physical activity partly inhibits autonomic imbalance, immune dysfunction and quality of life induced by chronic shiftwork in policemen.
articles.authors: Hélida C Aquino-Santos, Jeanne S Tavares-Vasconcelos, Anamei Silva-Reis et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic shiftwork can impair autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune homeostasis. However, the interaction between occupational status and physical activity level in military police officers remains incompletely understood. This cross-sectional factorial study included 102 men stratified according to occupational status and physical activity level: physically active military police officers (PMP; n = 26), physically inactive military police officers (PMNP; n = 26), physically active civilians (CVP; n = 25) and physically inactive civilians (CVNP; n = 25). Quality of life, perceived stress, sleepiness, haematological parameters, cytokines and heart rate variability were assessed. Physical activity improved several Short-form questionnaire (SF-36) domains, particularly Physical Functioning and General Health. Military police officers demonstrated lower mean normal-to-normal intervals and lower high-frequency power than civilians, indicating differences in resting autonomic cardiovascular modulation associated with occupational status. Serum interleukin-10 concentrations were significantly lower in military police officers, whereas interleukin-2, interleukin-17 and interferon-γ did not differ significantly according to occupational status. Haemoglobin levels and platelet counts demonstrated significant occupational status × physical activity interactions. Perceived stress scores were lower in military police officers than in civilians. Chronic occupational exposure to shiftwork was associated with altered autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune regulation in military police officers. Regular physical activity improved quality of life somewhat; however, several physiological alterations remained predominantly associated with occupational status, reinforcing the importance of occupational strategies targeting circadian health and physiological resilience. These findings highlight the physiological complexity of chronic shiftwork exposure in tactical occupational populations.

articles.title: Dimensionality Reduction of Full-Body Strength-Power Metrics to Identify Distinct Strength Domains in Elite Rugby Union Athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Leslie K D Payne, Matthew C Varley, David L Carey et al.
articles.abstract: Payne, LKD, Varley, MC, Carey, DL, Driller, MW, and James, LP. Dimensionality reduction of full-body strength-power metrics to identify distinct strength domains in elite rugby union athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to determine the extent of shared and unique information among strength tests and to evaluate whether factors identified through exploratory factor analysis reflect distinct strength domains in professional rugby union players. Twenty professional male rugby union athletes (age 24.4 ± 3.8 years; height 186.3 ± 5.2 cm; body mass 107.6 ± 10.9 kg) completed a battery of 4 upper-body and 5 lower-body isometric, dynamic, and reactive strength tests. A total of 18 metrics were entered into exploratory factor analysis to identify distinct strength domains. Exploratory factor analysis reduced the data set into 2 upper-body domains (pressing and pulling) and 4 lower-body domains (isometric, dynamic, reactive, and relative). These domains together explained 73% of the variance in the upper-body data and 79% of the variance in the lower-body data. The isometric domain was driven by early-phase force at 100 and 200 ms, while peak force contributed less strongly. The dynamic domain was defined by heavy squat velocity, which diverged inversely from countermovement jump height, reflecting load-velocity differences. The reactive domain was shaped by contact time and countermovement depth, highlighting the role of temporal mechanics. The relative domain was defined by drop jump height and countermovement jump momentum, emphasizing the influence of body mass on ballistic force expression. Eighteen test metrics were successfully reduced to 6 distinct domains of strength in professional rugby union athletes. This framework provides a concise basis for profiling upper-body and lower-body strength to reduce redundancy and retain key information needed for training and monitoring rugby athletes.

articles.title: The Relationship of Countermovement Jump Performance to Operational Readiness in United States Air Force Special Operators.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Sam T Tomlitz, Jay Dawes, Mark G Abel et al.
articles.abstract: Tomlitz, ST, Dawes, J, Abel, MG, and Potenza, MA. The relationship of countermovement jump performance to operational readiness in United States air force special operators. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-Operational readiness signifies the degree to which special operations soldiers are physically capable of accomplishing occupational tasks. The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between selected countermovement jump (CMJ)-derived neuromuscular performance characteristics and operational readiness assessment scores among United States Air Force Pararescuemen (PJs). Thirty-six male PJs (age = 37.06 ± 5.98 years, height = 178.73 ± 6.27 cm, body mass (BM) = 86.51 ± 8.97 kg, body mass index = 27.06 ± 2.24 kg/m2) performed a series of tests, including a CMJ test and components of the tier II Operator Fitness Test (OFT). The CMJ-derived metrics (jump height, concentric impulse (CI), reactive strength modified, peak power (PP), PP/BM, concentric peak force, peak landing force, landing impulse, CI asymmetry, countermovement depth, eccentric PP/BM, force at zero velocity) were correlated with the tier II OFT events using bivariate Spearman's correlations. The significance level of this study was set at ≤ 0.05. A large relationship was found between standing long jump and reactive strength index modified (RSImod) (rs = 0.62, p = 0.012). Multiple power variables correlated with farmer's carry sprint performance, including CI (rs = -0.59, p = 0.038), RSImod (rs = -0.64, p = 0.007), PP (rs = -0.71, p < 0.001), and relative PP (PP/BM) (rs = -0.74, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that specific performance characteristics may serve as useful indicators of task performance in the OFT assessment.

articles.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Miguel Gomes, Mara Costa, Pedro Pezarat-Correia et al.
articles.abstract: Gomes, M, Costa, M, Pezarat-Correia, P, and Mendonca, GV. Lower-body strength and hypertrophy adaptations in response to concurrent training in trained young males. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined the interference effect of concurrent training (CT) on maximal and explosive strength and muscle morphology in trained young males. Thirty subjects were randomly assigned to endurance training (E), resistance training (R), or CT for 11 weeks. The intervention comprised 2 mesocycles: weeks 1-5 emphasizing maximal strength, and weeks 6-11 targeting explosive strength. Assessments were conducted at baseline, mid-training, and post-training, and included leg-press maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC), rate of force development (RFD), countermovement jump kinetics, and vastus lateralis cross-sectional area and pennation angle. Maximal voluntary isometric contraction increased only in the R group (18.4 ± 10.2%, p = 0.015). Peak RFD improved in both R (31.8 ± 23.2%) and CT (23.1 ± 27.9%), although with distinct time courses: R improved progressively across both mesocycles, whereas CT improved only during the second. Early-phase RFD (0-50 ms) increased in the R group from mid-training onward, whereas the CT group improved only from mid- to post-training (38.3 ± 40.4%, p = 0.021), accompanied by greater quadriceps electromyographic activity (p < 0.05). No changes in RFD were observed in E during training. Countermovement jump positive impulse improved in both R (12.7 ± 9.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 8.3%, p < 0.05), with no evidence of interference in jump-related explosive performance. Cross-sectional area increased in both R (17.0 ± 13.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 9.4%, p < 0.05). Pennation angle increased in CT (10.1 ± 12.9%) and R (18.6 ± 15.1%). These findings indicate that, although CT may limit MVIC development and delay early-phase RFD adaptations, it does not hinder explosive performance when resistance training is oriented toward rapid-strength development. Thus, CT can be effectively implemented in trained individuals when resistance training is periodized to emphasize neural-driven explosive or hypertrophy-related adaptations.

articles.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Ramiro Chilingirian-Padrón, Tania Álvarez-Yates, Oscar García-García
articles.abstract: Chilingirian-Padrón, R, Álvarez-Yates, T, and García-García, O. Effects of in-season contrast strength training on jump performance and sprint ability in female field hockey players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 6-week in-season contrast strength training program incorporating sport-specific tasks on neuromuscular performance in sub-elite female field hockey players. Twenty-five athletes completed a pre-post single-cohort intervention integrated into their regular team schedule. Each session consisted of 3 sequential blocks: (a) a high-load strength exercise targeting maximal strength or hypertrophy (70-85% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]); (b) a biomechanically related explosive action performed at low load (∼30% 1RM) and high execution velocity; and (c) a high-speed sport-specific task. Jump performance was assessed using bilateral and unilateral countermovement jumps (CMJs) and free arm CMJ, whereas sprint ability was evaluated through 10- and 20-m sprints. A mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to determine the effects of the intervention, with Time (Pre, Post) as within-subject factor and Playing Position (defenders, midfielders, forwards) as between-subject factor, with the level of significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Significant improvements were observed in all jump and sprint assessments: jump performance increased by 5.7-29.6%, whereas sprint ability improved by 1.6-1.9%. These findings indicate that 6 weeks of contrast strength training incorporating high-speed sports-specific tasks performed during the competitive season elicited meaningful improvements in stretch-shortening cycle-related jump performance and sprint ability in sub-elite female field hockey players.

articles.title: Maximum Deceleration Is Related to Players' Ability to Repeat High-Intensity Decelerations in a Match in Female Professional Soccer Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: David Martínez-Hernández, Paul A Jones, José M Oliva-Lozano et al.
articles.abstract: Martínez-Hernández, D, Jones, PA, Oliva-Lozano, JM, and Harper, DJ. Maximum deceleration is related to players' ability to repeat high-intensity decelerations in a match in female professional soccer players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was twofold; First, to investigate positional differences in high-intensity decelerations (HID; < -3 m·s-2) and very high-intensity decelerations (VHID; < -4 m·s-2) in elite female soccer players. Second, to examine relationships between maximum deceleration (DMax) and the frequency of HID and VHID throughout competitive match play, reflecting players' capacity to perform these actions repeatedly. Twenty-four professional female outfield players (189 match files) from an English Women's Superleague club were tracked across 27 matches using 10-Hz Global Positioning System devices. Differences in deceleration metrics (DMax, HID, VHID) across positions were analyzed using 1-way analysis of variance and Bonferroni post hoc tests. Pearson's correlations assessed relationships between DMax, HID, and VHID across playing positions. Significant positional differences were observed. Central defenders had the lowest DMax and performed fewer HID and VHID actions than other positions, whereas central midfielder recorded the highest HID values. Maximum deceleration showed moderate-to-large correlations with HID (r = 0.35) and VHID (r = 0.52). Positional and individual variations influenced the strength of these relationships. This study provides novel evidence that maximal deceleration capacity is an important neuromuscular performance quality that distinguishes playing positions in elite women's soccer, with moderate-to-large associations with the ability to perform repeated HID and VHID supporting its relevance to match performance, particularly at higher intensities. These findings suggest that DMax may be an important quality to target through training, with potential implications for repeated deceleration performance. Practitioners should implement position-specific assessments and interventions to optimize deceleration capacity, especially as modern game demands continue to evolve.

articles.title: The Role of Physical Preparation in Motorsport Athletes Across Different Vehicle Types: A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Gabriel Vieira Barros, Ana Ramos, Maurício Facchini et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite motorsport's widespread appeal, early performance models did not consider drivers as athletes, and even drivers often struggled with this classification, which historically contributed to their exclusion from research focused on athletic performance. Slowly but steadily, this paradigm has been changing. PURPOSE: To review the evolution of physical conditioning in land-based motorsports and to examine the specific physiological and physical demands imposed on drivers by different vehicle types. A narrative review was conducted to synthesize historical perspectives, physiological demands, and training approaches in motorsport. Peer-reviewed studies, practical reports, opinion articles, and relevant online materials were analyzed to describe the evolution of the physical conditioning required across racing categories. The physical demands in motorsports are characterized by sustained cardiovascular strain, significant neuromuscular loading, large and sustained G-force exposure, and pronounced thermal stress. These demands vary according to vehicle type. Closed-wheel drivers are particularly exposed to prolonged heat stress and require comprehensive muscular endurance and thermoregulatory adaptation. Open-wheel drivers experience large G-forces, demanding exceptional neck and lower-limb strength. Two-wheel riders require enhanced handgrip strength, dynamic neuromuscular control, and high levels of aerobic capacity. CONCLUSIONS: Tailored conditioning programs addressing the distinct physiological, neuromuscular, and thermoregulatory demands of each motorsport category are closely linked to performance and safety. Further systematic evaluation of the empirical evidence is necessary to enhance the ecological validity of training recommendations and strengthen their application in competitive motorsport.

articles.title: Central and Peripheral Fatigue Following Free-Weight and Smith Machine Squat Training: Neuromuscular Efficiency in Knee Extensors.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Daniel Marcos-Frutos, Antonio Martos-Arregui, Amador García-Ramos et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Free-weight (FW) and machine-guided exercises have been shown to promote similar strength and hypertrophy adaptations. Under such conditions, the exercise modality that induces less fatigue may be considered more efficient and advantageous for training prescription. PURPOSE: To compare the mechanical, perceptual, and neuromuscular fatigue induced by a squat strength training session performed with FW or a Smith machine (SM). METHODS: Nineteen young strength-trained men (age = 23.5 [3.8] y; strength training experience = 4.7 [2.4] y) completed 2 sessions in a randomized order, each involving 4 sets of 9 repetitions at 70% 1-repetition maximum and differing only in the squat modality (FW or SM). Mechanical fatigue was assessed by velocity loss during training and by pre-post changes in isometric force; perceptual fatigue was assessed by subjectively estimated repetitions in reserve and neuromuscular fatigue (ie, peripheral and central fatigue components) via the twitch interpolation technique during isometric unilateral knee extension. RESULTS: No fatigue differences were observed for velocity loss or perceptual fatigue variables (P = .136-.313). In contrast, most peripheral and central fatigue variables showed significant posttraining differences (P < .001-.021), with FW squats promoting greater posttraining peripheral and central fatigue. CONCLUSIONS: Given the comparable adaptations typically reported for FW and SM exercises, the SM squat may represent a more efficient option for promoting strength adaptations while minimizing neuromuscular fatigue in knee extensors.

articles.title: Can Graded Blood Flow Restriction Pressure Enhance and Prolong Postactivation Performance Enhancement Induced by Plyometric Jumps?
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Liang Wang, Chengyu Ke, Olivier Girard et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study investigated whether adding blood flow restriction at graded arterial occlusion pressures (AOPs) during plyometric jumps can enhance and prolong postactivation performance enhancement. METHODS: Twenty-one resistance-trained men completed 40 maximal plyometric jumps under 4 conditions: jumps alone or combined with blood flow restriction at 50%, 60%, or 70% AOP. Countermovement jump (CMJ) and squat jump (SJ) height were assessed at baseline and at 15 seconds, 4, 8, and 12 minutes postexercise. RESULTS: Significant condition × time interactions were observed for both CMJ height (P = .01, ηp2=.13) and SJ height (P < .001, ηp2=.14). The 70% AOP condition produced significant performance improvements across all time points (P < .01, g = 0.36-0.53). At 50% and 60% AOP, performance improved at 15 seconds and 4 minutes (P < .01, g = 0.19-0.40), with CMJ effects persisting to 8 minutes but disappearing by 12 minutes in both jumps. The control condition showed a transient CMJ improvement at 15 seconds (P = .046, g = 0.20) but no SJ change. Compared with other conditions, 70% AOP outperformed control at 4 and 12 minutes for CMJ and at 12 minutes for SJ, and exceeded 50% AOP at 15 seconds in both tests. CONCLUSION: Plyometric jumps combined with 70% AOP produced a greater and more sustained postactivation performance enhancement response than jumps alone, suggesting that blood flow restriction may serve as a potential adjunct to enhance the acute effects of plyometric conditioning activities.

articles.title: Effects of Ballistic and Traditional Half-Squat Training With Light Loads on Strength, Jump, and Sprint Performance in Young Rugby Players: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Santiago Zabaloy, Piotr Zmijewski, Tomás T Freitas et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study examined the effects of two 6-week in-season training interventions using light loads (30%-40% 1-repetition maximum) and contrasting strategies: (1) ballistic jump squat (JS) and (2) traditional half squat on strength, jump, and sprint performance in youth rugby players. METHODS: Twenty-five highly trained players completed the randomized controlled trial, training 3 times per week alongside regular rugby practice and competition. Performance assessments included half-squat 1-repetition maximum, mean propulsive velocity, squat jump, countermovement jump, and 30-m sprint speed at 3 time points. RESULTS: Both groups improved maximal strength and jump performance, with greater gains observed in the JS group (≈7% vs 4% for strength, ≈16% vs 8% for jump performance). The JS group also showed specific improvements in relative strength and heavy-load mean propulsive velocity, whereas the half-squat group improved mean propulsive velocity at lighter loads. A significant group × time interaction was found for countermovement jump, favoring the JS condition. Despite these neuromuscular improvements, sprint performance decreased in both groups, with no between-group differences. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that light-load ballistic training may provide a more effective stimulus for improving strength and power qualities during the in-season period, likely due to its velocity-oriented and fully accelerative nature. However, strength-power gains alone appear insufficient to prevent decreases in sprint performance under congested fixture schedules. From a practical standpoint, incorporating light-load ballistic exercises may enhance neuromuscular performance while minimizing fatigue, but additional sprint-specific training is required to maintain or improve sprint speed in youth rugby players.

articles.title: The Effect of Environmental Temperature on Physical Performance, Physiological and Perceptual Responses in Elite Versus Nonelite Male Beach Soccer Players.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Thiago Carvalho, Vincenzo Rago, João Brito et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: High environmental temperature (Te) is associated with adverse effects on athletes' performance. Whether such effects are comparable across different sports and competitive levels remains uncertain. We explored and compared the physical performance, physiological, and perceptual responses of elite and nonelite beach soccer players during official matches, focusing on the potential effects of Te. METHODS: One hundred fifty-four male beach soccer players were monitored across 13 official matches. Physical performance (locomotor activity and countermovement jump), heart rate, rate of perceived exertion, hydration (liquid intake and fluid loss), and Te were collected. Data were analyzed using multivariate analysis of variance, followed by multivariate analysis of covariance and interaction analyses. RESULTS: Elite players covered greater total distance (∼16%), high-speed running (∼19%), and sprinting (∼60%); performed more sprints (∼60%) and had ∼1-point higher rate of perceived exertion than nonelite players. After adjustment for Te, differences in total distance and rate of perceived exertion between competitive levels appeared attenuated. In contrast, small effects were observed for Vpeak (ηp2=.037) and accelerations (ηp2=.030), and a medium effect was observed for fluid loss (ηp2=.076). As Te increased, elite players tended to cover greater total distance while reducing high-intensity actions, whereas nonelite players showed progressively greater high-intensity efforts, with relatively stable HRpeak and HRmean, while time >85%HRpeak tended to increase. In matches played at Te ≥ 35 °C, elite players experienced ∼34% greater fluid loss than nonelite players. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that elite and nonelite beach soccer players may respond differently as Te increases, highlighting the need for monitoring and hydration strategies tailored to competitive level under high Te conditions.

articles.title: What characteristics are associated with meeting the Canadian physical activity guidelines for people with multiple sclerosis? A retrospective chart review.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jillian Scandiffio, Sarah Munce, Sarah J Donkers et al.
articles.abstract: Meeting multiple sclerosis-specific physical activity guidelines (PAGs) has been associated with numerous benefits in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). However, the characteristics of PwMS predictive of meeting PAGs are unknown. This study aimed to examine which sociodemographic and clinical characteristics are associated with meeting the Canadian MS PAGs. A retrospective chart review of all PwMS referred to physiatry at the largest Canadian tertiary MS clinic between December 2021-December 2023 (n=455) was conducted. Physical activity, sociodemographic, and clinical characteristics were collected. Physical activity levels were categorized into one of three groups: no activity, some activity but not meeting PAGs, and meeting PAGs. Physical activity was further categorized by type of activity (aerobic and strength training). Associations between characteristics and physical activity levels were examined using multinomial logistic regression. PwMS who did not drive (OR=0.53, 95%CI=0.29-0.97) and were non-ambulatory (OR=0.34, 95%CI 0.11-0.99) were significantly less likely to meet PAGs. Higher Expanded Disability Status Scale (OR=0.80, 95% CI=0.70-0.91), gait aid use (OR=0.55, 95%CI=0.34-0.88), incoordination (OR= 0.52, 95% CI=0.33-0.82), progressive MS phenotype (OR=0.60, 95% CI=0.37-0.95), and smoking (OR=0.31, 95% CI=0.13-0.76) were associated with lower odds of doing any aerobic activity. Those with cognitive symptoms (OR=1.93, 95%CI=1.22-3.04) and greater muscle strength (OR=1.04, 95% CI=1.01-1.07) were more likely to do aerobic activity. Only employment status was associated with strength training, with those employed more likely to do some strength training (OR=1.73, 95% CI=1.04-2.89). Physical disability, cognitive symptoms, adverse health behaviours may drive which type and amount of activity a PwMS participates in.

articles.title: Determining the association between gender-related factors and the perception of exertional dyspnoea in healthy males and females.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jasvir K Dhaliwal, Jack R Dunsford, Gracie O Grift et al.
articles.abstract: The perception exertional dyspnoea is greater in females than males at absolute, but not relative, levels of minute ventilation (VE). The mechanisms of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea are unclear, but since dyspnoea perception is influenced by psychological, social, and cultural factors, it is possible that gender-related characteristics confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea. We sought to determine the association between gender-related characteristics and dyspnoea during exercise in males and females. Forty-six healthy adults (n=22 males, n=24 females) completed the Stanford Gender-related Variables for Health Research questionnaire to assess their gender-related characteristics (i.e., caregiver strain, work strain, independence, risk-taking, emotional intelligence, social support, and discrimination), spirometry, and an incremental cycle exercise test. Throughout exercise, standard cardiorespiratory parameters were monitored, and dyspnoea perception was assessed using the Borg scale. Females had significantly higher scores than males for emotional intelligence (p=0.029) and social support (p=0.049); whereas other gender-related characteristics were similar between the sexes (all p>0.05). Females reported significantly higher dyspnoea intensity and unpleasantness ratings than males at a V̇E of 80 l·min-1 (both p<0.05); however, males had higher dyspnoea intensity ratings at 20 and 40 % of maximum voluntary ventilation (MVV; both p<0.05). After adjusting for sex, height, body mass, and age, emotional intelligence was significantly associated with dyspnoea intensity at a V̇E of 50 l·min-1 and 50 %MVV (R2=0.14-0.18, all p<0.05). Our findings suggest that gender-related characteristics influence the perception of exertional dyspnoea, and may confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea perception.

articles.title: Dietary Supplement Use and Beliefs Among Athletes at the 2025 Canada Games.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jana Daher, Adriah Kate Sahajpal, Vijay Sahajpal et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary supplement use is widespread among athletes; however, limited data exist regarding supplement use and beliefs among Canadian youth athletes. This cross-sectional online study aimed to examine dietary supplement use and related beliefs among athletes competing at the 2025 Canada Games in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. A total of 473 respondents participated in the survey. Of the 473 participants, 385 completed responses to the dietary supplement (DS) questions. Among participants who reported their sex, 125 were male and 189 were female. Overall, 36% of participants reported current dietary supplement use. Supplement use was significantly higher among males than females (47% vs. 23%, p < .001) and increased with age (p = .001). The most commonly reported supplements were protein powder (49%), sports drinks (46%), and creatine (45%). Primary reasons for use included maintaining good health (76%), increasing energy (54%), and promoting recovery (50%). Coaches (50%) and healthcare professionals (49%) were the most frequently reported information sources. Supplement users demonstrated significantly stronger positive beliefs regarding benefits of dietary supplements compared with non-users (all p < .001). Ordinal logistic regression showed that supplement users had greater odds of stronger agreement that supplements improve performance (OR = 5.50, 95% CI: 3.31-9.13, p < .001). These findings highlight the use of dietary supplements among Canadian youth athletes and support the need for targeted nutrition education to promote informed decision-making.

articles.title: Anabolic inequality among whole protein foods.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Nicholas A Burd, Žan Zupančič, Daniel R Moore et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary protein consumption in optimization strategies for supporting muscle are shifting from isolated nutrient models to integrated food-first frameworks. This perspective examines the role of food matrix integrity in regulating the primary locus of control of muscle mass in health adults: muscle protein synthesis (MPS). We propose that food processing techniques alter the matrix's physical and chemical architecture, thereby modulating the anabolic potential of whole protein foods. Consequently, identifying optimal feeding strategies requires combining mechanistic insights with food-first approaches, acknowledging that food matrix integrity is a regulatory variable in MPS regulation in support of muscle health.

articles.title: Where are the female participants in resistance training and muscle hypertrophy research? A review of gender/sex representation.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Nathalia F Dias, Deivid G Silva, Julio Benvenutti Bueno de Camargo et al.
articles.abstract: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the representation of female participants in resistance training (RT) studies investigating hypertrophy and to assess associations between participant sex, methodological features, authorship, and temporal trends. This review included RT studies published in peer-reviewed journals that assessed hypertrophy outcomes in young adults. Reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on participant sex, menstrual cycle phase reporting/consideration, use of molecular or biopsy analyses, and gender/sex of first and last authors. A total of 570 studies were included. Of these, 72.2% recruited male participants, 11.0% female participants, and 16.8% included both sexes. Among studies including female participants, 8.5% reported or accounted for menstrual cycle phase, while 87.3% did not mention it. Molecular analyses were nearly four times more frequent in studies with only male participants (23.6%) than those including female participants (6.5%; χ²=9.45; p<0.009). No association was found between participant sex and use of muscle biopsies or author gender/sex. A 10-fold increase in RT publications occurred in the 21st vs. 20th century, yet the sex gap persisted. Studies published in 2020-June 2023 showed modest improvement versus 2001-2019, with fewer male-only and more female-only and mixed-sex samples (χ²=16.43; p=0.00027; Cramér's V=0.18). Despite growing evidence that females and males exhibit broadly similar relative hypertrophy and molecular responses to RT, substantial sex bias persists in hypertrophy research. Although studies published since 2020 show modest improvement in sex-inclusive recruitment, male-only designs still predominate, and limited menstrual cycle phase reporting/accounting continues to constrain transparency and generalizability.

articles.title: A multimodal deep learning model for classifying early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head on biparametric MRI.
articles.authors: Siyuan Li, Huimin Huang, Yetong He et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Precise early- versus late-stage stratification of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is critical for hip-preserving treatment selection, yet conventional MRI interpretation suffers from interobserver variability and limited objectivity. This study aimed to develop a multimodal deep learning model integrating biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE) with clinical parameters (including age, sex, affected side (left, right, or bilateral), and etiology) to differentiate early- from late-stage ONFH and provide objective imaging evidence. METHODS: This retrospective study included 530 patients with ONFH, yielding imaging data from 851 hips. The collected data comprised STIR sequences, T1-FSE sequences, and clinical information, including age, sex, and etiology. The dataset was randomly divided at the patient level into a training set (424 patients, 675 hips) and a test set (106 patients, 176 hips) at an 8:2 ratio. Seven models were constructed: a clinical model, a STIR model, a T1-FSE model, a bpMRI model, a STIR-clinical model, a T1-FSE-clinical model, and a bpMRI-clinical model. Early- and late-fusion strategies were used for multimodal integration. The diagnostic performance of the seven models for classifying early- versus late-stage ONFH was systematically compared, with particular emphasis on their ability to identify borderline cases at the transition between clinical stages. Model interpretability was assessed using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). RESULTS: The early-fusion bpMRI-clinical model achieved the highest AUC of 0.944 (95% CI 0.905-0.973), accuracy 90.9%, sensitivity 89.0%, and specificity 92.9%, significantly outperforming single-sequence models (all P < 0.05). The confusion matrix showed that the model misclassified 10 late-stage cases as early-stage and 6 early-stage cases as late-stage. Grad-CAM visualizations indicated that the model primarily focused on clinically relevant regions, including the necrotic lesion boundary, areas of bone marrow edema, and subchondral structural abnormalities. These attention patterns were highly consistent with the core imaging features used for early- versus late-stage ONFH stratification. CONCLUSION: This study presents an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates dual-sequence MRI with clinical parameters. The framework accurately differentiates early- from late-stage ONFH according to the ARCO classification and provides objective evidence for determining the critical threshold for hip-preservation decision-making. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No: ChiCTR2300075354. Sep 1, 2023).

articles.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Hongbo Wen, Ting Zhang, Tingting Xie et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Affecting 21-35% of patients after total knee arthroplasty (TKA), kinesiophobia critically impedes postoperative rehabilitation. Whether exercise-based interventions reduce kinesiophobia more effectively than routine postoperative rehabilitation remains unclear. METHODS: We systematically searched 11 databases from inception to July 11, 2026, for RCTs comparing exercise-based rehabilitation with routine postoperative rehabilitation in adults undergoing primary TKA. The primary outcome was kinesiophobia. Secondary outcomes included knee function, pain, balance, mobilization time, and adherence. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Eleven RCTs (N = 1,096) were included. Exercise-based rehabilitation was associated with a reduction in kinesiophobia (SMD = - 1.22, 95% CI [- 1.72, - 0.72]; I2 = 93%; low certainty) and improvements in knee function (SMD = 1.19, 95% CI [0.67, 1.71]; I2 = 93%; low certainty). For pain, the ≤ 4-week pooled estimate (SMD = - 1.09, 95% CI [- 2.03, - 0.14]; I2 = 94%) was not interpretable due to extreme heterogeneity and was not robust: after exclusion of the single acute in-hospital trial, the confidence interval crossed zero (SMD = - 1.09, 95% CI [- 2.28, 0.09]). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses otherwise supported the directional conclusions for kinesiophobia and knee function, although effect sizes were unstable and certainty remained low. CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that exercise-based rehabilitation may be associated with reductions in kinesiophobia at ≤ 4 weeks and an interpretable 12-week improvement in knee function after TKA; the ≤ 4-week and ≥ 24-week functional subgroup estimates were not interpretable because of extreme heterogeneity, and the early pain signal was possible but non-robust. Effect sizes should be interpreted with caution due to substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias, and sensitivity to outlying studies. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs with rigorous blinding and standardized protocols are urgently needed.

articles.title: The impact of work-related foot pain on work and personal life: an interview study.
articles.authors: Ann-Sophie Hörnell, Anncristine Fjellman-Wiklund, Åsa Svedmark et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The occurrence of foot pain is high, especially in those with physically demanding occupations. Work-related foot pain has been shown to impact work performance, family life, and leisure activities. While prevalence across various sectors is documented, research exploring experiences and total life impact of work-related foot pain remains limited. AIM: The aim of this study was to explore experiences of living with foot pain among individuals employed in highly demanding physical occupations, and occupations characterised by prolonged standing or walking. METHODS: A qualitative, semi-structured interview-based approach was chosen. Twelve individual interviews were conducted with nine women and three men, and analysed using Qualitative Content Analysis. RESULTS: One main theme, Walking a fine line - Balancing challenges in multiple aspects of life due to work-related foot pain, and three sub-themes were identified, describing how external work-environment factors and internal experiences of autonomy impact an individual's overall life situation, including impact on family life and the mental toll of living and working with foot pain. The sub-theme Struggling with increased pain due to work conditions and environment highlights how factors such as certain types of floors, physical work demands, time spent on the feet, walking, heavy lifting, and inadequate footwear directly exacerbate pain. The sub-theme Feeling like just another cog in the machine due to limited control over workplace organisation reflects difficulties for employees in influencing work tasks, planning daily work tasks and responsibilities, a lack of recovery during the workday, and communication within the workplace. The sub-theme Experiencing inequality and low quality of life outside of work describes the consequences for individuals' personal lives, including restricted social participation, strained family relations, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances. Overall, the individuals expressed a sense of resignation, feeling that they had to "grit their teeth" and continue working despite the pain. CONCLUSION: The central findings of this study are negative experiences and struggles, during both work and leisure time. Understanding the experiences of individuals with work-related foot pain can help employers and healthcare providers to identify work-related risks and consider preventative measures, although further research on this topic is needed. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Transition from open surgery to ultrasound-guided minimally invasive surgery for insertional Achilles tendinopathy: similar patient-reported outcomes and substantially lower treatment costs.
articles.authors: Louise Lindén, Håkan Alfredson, Maziar Mohaddes et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy is commonly treated surgically when conservative management fails. Traditionally, open central-splitting surgery (OCS) has been the standard approach, but minimally invasive ultrasound-guided techniques have recently been introduced. This study compared patient-reported outcomes and treatment costs following a transition in surgical practice from open central-splitting surgery to ultrasound- and colour Doppler-guided minimally invasive wide-awake local anaesthesia no tourniquet (WALANT) surgery. METHODS: This retrospective historical cohort study included fifty-two consecutive patients with insertional Achilles tendinopathy. Twenty patients underwent OCS surgery during 2017-2019, followed by thirty-two patients who underwent US-/CD-guided WALANT surgery during 2020-2022. The primary clinical outcome was the SEFAS score at 12 months. Between-group differences in the 12-month SEFAS scores were analysed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for baseline SEFAS score, age, sex, and BMI. Direct medical costs were estimated from the resource use observed across the two treatment pathways. RESULTS: The mean SEFAS score improved from 18 at baseline to 40 at 12 months in the US-/CD group and from 23 to 41 in the OCS group. In the adjusted analysis, the mean difference in the 12-month SEFAS was 0.62 points in favour of US-/CD (95% CI, - 3.50 to 4.73). Estimated direct medical costs were $1,432 per patient for US-/CD and $3,343 for OCS, corresponding to an absolute reduction of $1,911 per patient and approximately 50% lower costs with the US-/CD treatment pathway. CONCLUSIONS: Following a transition in surgical practice, US-/CD-guided surgery was associated with similar 12-month patient-reported outcomes and approximately 50% lower direct medical costs compared with OCS surgery. These findings suggest that minimally invasive US-/CD-guided surgery under local anaesthesia may offer a less resource-intensive alternative for the surgical treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Preoperative factors associated with quadriceps strength 1 year after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Per Sjöström, Lena Nordeman, Ola Rolfson et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Quadriceps strength is highly related to physical function following total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Preoperative factors associated with long-term postoperative strength remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this exploratory study was to investigate preoperative factors associated with normalized quadriceps strength (NQS), changes in NQS and limb symmetry index (LSI) 1 year after TKA in patients with uncomplicated recovery. METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Measurements took place at three primary care rehabilitation facilities in Region Västra Götaland, Sweden. The final analysis included 39 participants aged 65 years or older who underwent elective fast-track primary TKA due to knee osteoarthritis and had an uncomplicated recovery. Preoperative factors associated with NQS in the operated limb after 1 year (n = 39), changes in NQS from preoperative testing to 1 year after TKA (n = 39), and LSI (n = 35) were analyzed in three separate exploratory multiple linear regression models. Preoperative factors included age, sex, NQS, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), and the LSI. RESULTS: Preoperative NQS (B = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.40 to 1.0, p < 0.001) and LSI (B = - 0.17, 95% CI: - 0.29 to - 0.037, p = 0.013) were significantly associated with NQS 1 year after TKA. LSI was the only preoperative factor significantly associated with changes in NQS (B = - 0.19, 95% CI: - 0.32 to - 0.059, p = 0.006) and LSI 1 year after TKA (B = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.15 to 0.68, p = 0.004). CONCLUSIONS: In this selected and relatively small sample, greater normalized quadriceps strength in the operated limb and higher LSI 1 year after TKA appeared to be primarily associated with higher preoperative normalized quadriceps strength in the operated limb and higher preoperative LSI, respectively, whereas strength gains appeared to be associated with lower preoperative LSI. The findings should be considered exploratory and primarily applicable to older adults with uncomplicated recovery after TKA. Confirmation in larger studies is warranted. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Retrospectively registered February 9, 2022 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov , ID: NCT05248815).

articles.title: News from the Foundation for Physical Therapy Research, October 2026.
Strategies to Manage Missed Appointments in Private Physical Therapy: A National Cross-Sectional Study of Use and Perceived Effectiveness.
articles.authors: Franck Peter, François-Régis Sarhan
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Missed appointments disrupt outpatient care and may be particularly consequential in private physical therapy, where continuity of care, appointment management, and fee-for-service remuneration are closely linked. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify strategies used by private physical therapists to manage missed appointments and assess their perceived effectiveness. DESIGN: This study used a national cross-sectional online survey design. SETTING: The study was conducted in private outpatient physical therapist practice in France. PARTICIPANTS: Participants were physical therapists working in private outpatient practice who completed an anonymous online questionnaire. EXPOSURE: The strategies examined included organizational, communication, and digital reminder strategies used to manage missed appointments. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes included the perceived effectiveness of strategies assessed using a 4-point Likert scale; responses to 3 predefined statements concerning relational and emotional effects; and exploratory association between digital reminder use and perceived overall effectiveness. RESULTS: A total of 1246 physical therapists participated. Online booking platform reminders were rated as effective or very effective by 78.9% of users (95% CI = 74.1%-83.2%), and SMS reminders by 77.7% (95% CI = 72.4%-82.9%). In-clinic posters received lower ratings (20.0%; 95% CI = 16.6%-23.4%). Digital reminder use was weakly associated with higher perceived overall effectiveness (Cramér V = 0.105). Respondents frequently agreed that missed appointments affected their relationship with the patient concerned (82.9%) and that they had experienced frustration or anger after a missed appointment (91.3%); 46.2% agreed that these feelings influenced their interactions with patients more generally. Exploratory content analysis of open-ended responses identified financial deterrents, organizational and reminder strategies, attendance rules, communication and patient education, and restriction or discontinuation of care after repeated absences. CONCLUSIONS: Digital reminders were perceived as the most effective strategies for managing missed appointments, but objective attendance outcomes were not assessed. Relational and emotional findings should be interpreted cautiously because they were based on 3 directionally framed, nonvalidated statements. RELEVANCE: Future studies should evaluate strategies using objective attendance data and balanced measures.

articles.title: Discharge Decision Making and the Contemporary Weighting of Clinical and Contextual Factors: A Survey of Acute Care Physical Therapists.
articles.authors: James P Crick, Thomas Gus Almonroeder, Tricia Widenhoefer
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Physical therapists routinely make discharge recommendations for patients in the hospital, yet the reasoning that drives these decisions is poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to describe contemporary acute care physical therapists' discharge reasoning and examine associations between reasoning constructs and recommended discharge intensity. DESIGN: This study used a cross-sectional clinical vignette-based survey. Therapists provided a discharge recommendation and supporting rationale. Free-text rationales were analyzed using directed content analysis, and quantitative associations between coded reasoning constructs and discharge recommendation intensity were examined using regression modeling. SETTING: The survey was conducted electronically with United States physical therapists practicing in hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: Participants were eighty-nine acute care physical therapists who completed discharge recommendations and free-text rationales for 10 vignettes. INTERVENTIONS: none. MAIN OUTCOMES: The three main outcomes for this study included: (1) Frequency and co-occurrence of coded reasoning constructs; (2) therapist-level reasoning profiles; and (3) associations between constructs and discharge intensity. RESULTS: Across 1604 construct code applications, 3 constructs dominated discharge reasoning: therapist prior experience (29.6%), patient functioning and disability (26.3%), and patient life context (25.3%). The majority (69.7%) of therapists demonstrated mixed reasoning patterns while less than one-third demonstrated a dominant reasoning profile. Patient functioning and disability was the only construct statistically associated with recommending more intensive post-acute care in ordered (OR = 1.70; 95% CI = 1.22-2.39) and binary (OR = 2.21; 95% CI = 1.30-3.74) models. CONCLUSIONS: Acute care discharge reasoning concentrates on functional status, professional experience, and patient life context, with other domains functioning mainly as situational amplifiers. RELEVANCE: A refined framework for discharge reasoning may support clearer interdisciplinary communication, inform targeted education, and guide efforts to optimize post-acute care utilization.

articles.title: Effect of Pain Science Education and Behavioral Graded Activity on Pain in Survivors of Breast Cancer: A Study Protocol for a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Astrid Lahousse, Eva Roose, Laurence Leysen et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Pain affects up to half of survivors of breast cancer and is one of the most common long-term consequences of cancer treatment, yet it remains under-recognized and undertreated. Pharmacological options often provide limited relief and may cause adverse effects. Evidence from other pain populations supports a biopsychosocial approach combining pain education and physical activity. OBJECTIVE: The objective is to evaluate whether pain science education (PSE) with behavioral graded activity (BGA) versus usual care (UC), reduces pain intensity and interference in survivors of breast cancer with pain. Secondary aims include assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and central pain modulation. DESIGN: This study is a multicenter, two-arm, assessor- and statistician-blinded, randomized controlled superiority trial. SETTING: The trial will be conducted in Belgium, with interventions delivered in hospital and academic research settings. PARTICIPANTS: Two hundred women with a history of breast cancer and persistent pain will be recruited. INTERVENTIONS: Participants will be randomized to either (1) PSE (1 session) plus 5 BGA sessions delivered by a trained physical therapist, or (2) usual care with a standardized biomedical pain information leaflet, over a 12-week period. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome will be pain intensity and interference (Brief Pain Inventory). Secondary outcomes will include HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30) and central pain modulation (Quantitative Sensory Testing). Exploratory outcomes include sleep, fatigue, pain-related cognitions, and health care utilization. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and at 3-month (primary endpoint), 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups. CONCLUSIONS: This trial will determine whether a structured PSE+BGA program improves pain and HRQoL in survivors of breast cancer, offering a potential scalable non-pharmacological treatment. RELEVANCE: These findings may guide targeted rehabilitation strategies and strengthen the role of physical therapists in managing post-cancer pain, particularly in light of the growing population of survivors of breast cancer and the increasing prevalence of persistent symptoms.
